title: USGS earthquakes (ComCat) and Water Data (streamflow, groundwater)
agency: U.S. Geological Survey (U.S. Department of the Interior)
questions: earthquakes of magnitude 5 or more in California since 2000
how many earthquakes hit Oklahoma each year
daily streamflow of the Potomac River last year
current river levels in a state
groundwater level trend at a well

key_only: more than a few water-data requests an hour (an api.data.gov key allows about 1,000 an hour); earthquakes never need a key

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser and save the JSON under the name shown (earthquakes: add &format=csv for CSV; water: change f=json to f=csv), then upload. Without the links: earthquakes at https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/ (Output Options > CSV); water at https://waterdata.usgs.gov (site page > Download data).

cache.why: Earthquake locations and magnitudes are revised for days to months and provisional water data change; data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: USGS data are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105; https://www.usgs.gov/information-policies-and-instructions/copyrights-and-credits); credit the USGS.

clarify: Which magnitude threshold and area (circle or box)? Counts depend strongly on both; small events are missing from older years.
Provisional or only approved water data? Recent values are provisional (approval_status) and may be revised.
